description.value: The study investigated whether perceptual guesses and internally generated free decisions share neural representations, using fMRI searchlight pattern classification and cross-condition prediction.

design.value: Event-related fMRI study in which participants made category choices about pianos and chairs under high visibility, zero-visibility perceptual guessing, and free-choice conditions.

description.value: Questionnaire assessing adherence to task instructions, awareness of the missing object images, and the timing and nature of free decisions.
Normal or corrected to normal visual acuity.

source_definition.value: The three experimental conditions were high visibility, perceptual guessing, and free decision.

levels.value: high visibility condition, perceptual guessing condition, free decision condition

source_definition.value: Trials were assigned to piano- and chair-trials according to participants' choices.

description.value: Sixteen right-handed participants with normal or corrected to normal visual acuity gave written informed consent and participated in the study. One participant indicated that he had noticed the missing object images and was excluded. The data from the remaining 15 participants were used for the analyses.

inclusion_criteria.value: normal or corrected to normal visual acuity

task_name.value: category choices about pianos and chairs

task_description.value: Participants made category choices about pianos and chairs using three different conditions: high visibility perceptual choices, zero-visibility perceptual guesses, and free choices.

instructions.value: Participants were asked to identify the category of the presented object, to make perceptual guesses about the poorly visible object, or to spontaneously and freely choose either “piano” or “chair”, whatever category came first to their minds.

stimuli.value: Twenty-four pictures of pianos and chairs, grey-scale images presented with forward and backward masks; the invisibility and free-choice conditions used a scrambled phase-texture noise image.

task_performance_measures.value: hit rate for visible pianos and chairs

instrument.value: Siemens TRIO 3 T scanner (Erlangen, Germany) with a standard head coil

description.value: Functional MRI volumes of the whole brain were acquired using gradient-echo EPI. Forty-two axial slices were acquired. Within each of the six runs, 208 volumes were acquired for each participant. The first two volumes of every scan were discarded by default to allow for magnetic saturation effects.

Motion corrected and unsmoothed brain images were used for a general linear model. Parameter estimates were normalized to a standard stereotaxic space using the Montreal Neurological Institute EPI template and smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 6 mm FWHM.

steps.value: no spatial smoothing before the first-level GLM
normalization to a standard stereotaxic space using the Montreal Neurological Institute EPI template
smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of 6 mm FWHM

description.value: All volumes were motion corrected to the first volume of the first run, normalized to MNI space, re-sampled to a voxel size of 3 × 3 × 3 mm3, and smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 8 mm FWHM.

steps.value: motion correction to the first volume of the first run
re-sampling to a voxel size of 3 × 3 × 3 mm3
smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of 8 mm FWHM

model_settings.value: Trials were modelled as events beginning with presentation of the cue, separately for piano and chair trials, for each run and condition.
Searchlight spheres had a radius of 4 voxels. The classifier used a fixed regularisation parameter C = 1 and six-fold cross-validation, training on all runs but one and testing on the remaining run.

level.value: individual participant level with random-effects group-level analyses

model_settings.value: Voxel-by-voxel analyses identified searchlight positions where local patterns had significant decoding accuracy across all participants.

description.value: On each trial one clearly visible piano or chair image was shown. Participants categorized the presented object.

Only a strongly masked neutral noise image was presented, creating the impression that an object was present without revealing its identity. Participants made a perceptual guess between piano and chair.

The same stimulus sequence as in the perceptual guessing condition was presented, but participants were instructed to spontaneously choose the category that first came to mind, independently of the presentation.
One of the two category choices.
One of the two category choices.

name.value: High visibility choices could exclusively be decoded from the LOC

spatial_scope.value: searchlight positions across the whole brain

role.value: greater decoding accuracy for piano versus chair choices
lesser side of the piano-versus-chair contrast

definition.value: decoding the category of highly visible object stimuli, distinguishing piano and chair choices

interpretations.value: the category of highly visible object stimuli was encoded in the bilateral visual cortex/LOC

definition.value: decoding the choice outcome of perceptual guesses, distinguishing pianos from chairs

interpretations.value: the medial posterior parietal cortex/precuneus encoded choices under perceptual guessing

roi_label.value: medial parietal cortex and anterior medial prefrontal cortex

definition.value: decoding outcomes of free decisions, distinguishing pianos from chairs

value.value: 57% in medial parietal cortex; 64% in anterior medial prefrontal cortex

interpretations.value: outcomes of free decisions were encoded in the medial parietal cortex and anterior medial prefrontal cortex

name.value: Cross-condition classification from perceptual guessing to free decision

definition.value: patterns from perceptual guessing were used to train the classifier to distinguish piano and chair choices and predict decisions in the free decision condition

generalization.value: trained on perceptual guessing and tested on free decisions

interpretations.value: activation patterns for guesses and free decisions in these regions allowed for the prediction of outcomes from one type of decision from activation patterns associated with the other

name.value: Cross-condition classification from free decision to perceptual guessing

definition.value: patterns from free decisions were used to train the classifier to distinguish piano and chair choices and predict decisions in the perceptual guessing condition

generalization.value: trained on free decisions and tested on perceptual guessing

interpretations.value: activation patterns for guesses and free decisions in these regions allowed for the prediction of outcomes from one type of decision from activation patterns associated with the other

name.value: Inclusive conjunction of bidirectional cross-condition classification

definition.value: an inclusive conjunction test requiring both directions of cross-condition prediction to be significant
guesses could be predicted from classifiers trained on free choices
free choices could be predicted from classifiers trained on perceptual guesses

interpretations.value: this finding supports the hypothesis of a similar neural code for guesses and free decisions in the medial posterior parietal cortex
